items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: there was a man named Septimus © Fillius Jazz Archive -16- Winner who published The Eureka Method.

ctx.x: Boy the person who arranged that must have known what the guitar was capable of.

Well that particular composer, Dan Foliart, who I’ve worked with for over 30 years, he did “Roseanne,” “Home Improvement,” a lot of shows. We did a show for 11 years called “Seventh Heaven” where the acoustic guitar was extremely prominent. Finger style acoustic guitar. And he was always write in different tunings. But he knows the instrument. But how do you notate that? You can’t write tablature because the copyists wouldn’t know what to do with it. So we worked out a system where he would write it in standard…

Winner who published The Eureka Method. And if you bought a guitar from Montgomery Ward or Sears, you would get this Eureka Method that would come with it. And so a lot of people learned how to play an open G tuning and you only need one finger to make chords. And you can play primary chords, open string, fifth fret, seventh fret. So yeah, I mean somebody that’s heading in the direction of a 12-bar blues will use that. And you can play — one of the things I do in my presentation is play the “Spanish Fandango” and…
